one_line: British brigadier-general who ordered the Jallianwala Bagh massacre in Amritsar, 1919.

appearance.age_look: mid-50s, medium height, solid but not bulky build, slightly stiff military bearing
appearance.face: Angular, long face with pronounced jaw, pale British complexion with light sun-weathering, narrow grey-blue eyes under slightly hooded lids, straight medium-length nose, thin pursed lips, neatly trimmed dark blond to light brown moustache; default expression is cold, controlled, and stern, with a hint of severity.
appearance.hair: Short, neatly parted dark blond to light brown hair, combed back from the forehead with a tidy left-side parting; hair kept close at the sides and slightly thicker on top, no visible sideburns; wearing a khaki service cap with a brown leather peak, khaki top, and a simple dark band, bearing a small, understated metal regimental badge at the front.
appearance.costume: Early 20th‑century British Indian Army khaki service uniform: a long‑sleeved, neatly pressed khaki tunic with four patch pockets and scalloped flaps, brass buttons down the front, and simple shoulder straps bearing rank pips; khaki cloth belt with a brown leather Sam Browne cross‑strap running diagonally from right shoulder to left hip; khaki trousers (straight cut, tucked smoothly into puttees), olive‑khaki wool puttees wrapped from ankle to mid‑calf; sturdy brown leather lace‑up boots; minimal adornment, but a wristwatch with a brown leather strap on the left wrist and a small, neat row of service ribbons above the left breast pocket; no cloak or greatcoat, emphasizing the crisp, light khaki of the hot-weather uniform.
appearance.signature: A long, polished wooden swagger stick with a dark brown shaft and a small metal tip, held firmly in one hand as a symbol of rigid authority rather than a combat weapon.

ref_desc: Reginald Dyer is a mid‑50s, pale British officer with a long angular face, narrow grey‑blue eyes, a neat dark blond moustache, short side‑parted hair under a khaki service cap, wearing a crisp khaki British Indian Army tunic, trousers, puttees, brown leather Sam Browne belt and boots, and carrying a dark brown wooden swagger stick, in a palette of dusty khaki, pale beige, dark brown leather, muted olive and steel grey‑blue.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full‑body anime‑style character sheet of Reginald Dyer as a British brigadier‑general in Amritsar, 1919: a mid‑50s, medium‑height man with a long angular pale face, narrow grey‑blue eyes, straight nose, thin lips and a neat dark blond to light brown moustache, his short hair parted on the left and combed back, partly hidden under a khaki service cap with a brown leather peak and a small metal badge at the front. Show him with a cold, stern default expression and stiff, formal posture. He wears an early 20th‑century British Indian Army hot‑weather khaki uniform: a long‑sleeved four‑pocket khaki tunic with brass buttons and simple shoulder straps bearing rank pips, a khaki cloth belt with a brown leather Sam Browne cross‑strap from right shoulder to left hip, straight‑cut khaki trousers tucked into olive‑khaki puttees wrapped from ankle to mid‑calf, and sturdy brown leather lace‑up boots. Add a small row of service ribbons above the left breast pocket and a plain wristwatch with a brown leather strap on his left wrist. In one hand he holds a long, dark brown polished wooden swagger stick with a small metal tip, used as a symbol of rigid authority. Keep the palette to dusty khaki, pale beige, dark brown leather, muted olive and steel grey‑blue, and present him front‑on with slight turn to show the Sam Browne strap, clearly displaying his face, hair, full uniform, boots and swagger stick for consistent redrawing.
